findings.summary: The plan endpoint and copilot_plan response field are not evidenced by a cited repository document or existing code, so the planner would implement an unverified internal-API contract and a stub could pass regardless of real-account correctness.
findings.evidence: The cited `docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md`, lines 623-643, documents only GET https://api.githubcopilot.com/models and its fields. A repository search for `copilot_internal/user` or `copilot_plan`, excluding this brief, returned no matches.
findings.fix: Before planning, confirm the endpoint and response field on a real account and add that experiment/result to a cited repository document, or explicitly record the operator's approval of this internal-API assumption in the brief.

findings.section: Behaviour contract > M2 — the id checked where it is set, and in doctor
findings.summary: The doctor row does not define its result when an id is locally knowable as a Claude alias but the models call fails or no login is available; the brief simultaneously promises an alias problem and a warning for call failure/no login.
findings.evidence: M2 states that any not-listed, disabled, or Claude-alias model is a problem naming each, but immediately says that a failed call or no login produces a warning. No literal alias entry is given for the doctor row. The model aliases can be detected without the API, and current `internal/cli/doctor.go:337-348` also distinguishes token availability before adding other rows.
findings.fix: Pin the precedence and literal doctor-row text for a Claude alias, including the case where the API is unreachable or no token exists: for example, whether the alias is a problem while the failed API is additionally warned elsewhere, or whether the new models row is warning-only. Keep it consistent with the existing unchanged `copilot login` row.

findings.summary: The close shape says to run the worked example line by line, but its setup includes `vloop init`, which the verify fence cannot run, without naming an end-to-end test or gate that covers that setup.
findings.evidence: The worked example prefaces the scratch repository with `vloop init` run; Shape task 6 runs the example line by line. The review guidelines bind: verify cannot run `vloop init`, and such a line must be covered by a named test with stubs or moved to operator acceptance.
findings.fix: Name the committed stubbed end-to-end test or final gate that performs the init precondition, or reframe the example around a test-created repository fixture and state explicitly what verify does not run.

decisions: Doctor/preflight checks Copilot ids with a short timeout and shows the account plan; I agree, subject to retaining the API-unreachable warning behavior.
Several session kinds are configured with `--kinds`; I agree.
Use the GitHub-internal plan endpoint and `copilot_plan` field; this needs operator confirmation because the cited repository evidence covers only the models endpoint.
Use five-second config/doctor calls and twenty-second list calls; recorded as an author choice for operator approval.
Use `VLOOP_COPILOT_API_URL` and `VLOOP_GITHUB_API_URL` as test-only endpoint overrides; recorded as an author choice for operator approval.
Treat `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, and `fable` as Claude aliases; recorded as an author choice for operator approval.
Make picker-enabled models the default list, expose every entry through `--all`, and return missing policy as `-`/null; I agree.
Make `--kinds` all-or-nothing and accept `plan, gate-review, work, review, second-review, verify, review-brief`; I agree.
checked: facts, consistency, rules, runnability; the ready-copy brief check passed with no warnings
